source.title: Hyperloop Transformers
source.authors: Abbas Zeitoun; Lucas Torroba Hennigen; Yoon Kim

record.tranche_reason: The study compares held-out perplexity across language-model architectures and varies loop count, but it does not fit or test the scaling laws in the claim. These comparisons bear on the architecture-sensitivity version using a different experimental setup.
record.gate_note: The study reports held-out perplexity for architecture comparisons and loop-count variations, and aggregate downstream accuracy across model sizes. It does not fit power laws, test extrapolation from small runs, or search for compute-optimal parameter/token allocations. The Chinchilla token count is used to set training tokens, not tested as a result. Related-work claims are not this study's results.
record.test_reason: Nearly parameter-matched architecture comparisons directly bear on V4. Downstream results across three training scales bear on the improvement-with-scale part of V6, although predictive accuracy is not evaluated. Chinchilla allocation is used to choose training budgets rather than tested.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate for the main experiments: Hyperloop improves parameter efficiency, remains competitive after INT4 quantization, and adds little measured training overhead; larger-scale generalization remains uncertain. Add the Appendix C qualification: with alternative initialization and tuned learning rates, Hyperloop matches rather than outperforms the Transformer baseline, while still improving on ordinary Looped.
record.recipe_differences: This is an architecture comparison, not a reproduction of the scaling-law fitting or compute-optimal allocation methods. It varies architecture and loop count and reports held-out perplexity.
record.method_sensitivity: Perplexity comparisons vary with architecture, loop count, model size, training-token setting, and quantization precision.

fits_no_version.finding: Depth-matched Hyperloop models achieve competitive perplexity with roughly half the parameters of ordinary Transformers.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Looping with hyper-connections improves parameter efficiency at matched unrolled depth and training-token count.

record.problems: No uncertainty estimates are reported. Experiments use FineWeb-Edu and reach at most the reported 2B-scale non-looped models; the authors identify scale as a limitation. Figure 2 values are available only graphically. The paper's Appendix C also reports a different initialization and tuning setting in which Hyperloop matches but does not outperform the Transformer baseline.
record.rows_left_out: Omitted Table 9's per-task accuracies, Tables 3-7's architecture ablations, Table 8's representation-similarity measurements, Figure 4's logit-lens measurements, and Table 10/Appendix C's alternative initialization results to stay within 60 rows. These are in Appendix B, Sections 4.3-4.4, and Appendix C; Table 10 reports a relevant alternative-setting result but is not included.

untested.parts: Power-law form over several orders of magnitude, with other resources non-bottlenecking; decreasing perplexity across a few configurations does not test this.
Prediction of much larger runs from power laws fitted on small runs.
Fixed-compute loss minimization and stable parameter/token allocation exponents.
Broad depth/width sweeps, a wide architecture range, and generalization beyond the tested scales. Figure 2's loss-change magnitude cannot be recovered from the supplied text.
Power-law form in other modalities or training regimes; overtraining and quantization comparisons do not establish that form.
Quantitative predictive fits, prediction of unseen scales, and a calibrated mapping from pretraining loss to downstream performance.
Dependence of fitted scaling exponents or compute-optimal splits on setup and fitting choices, and departures from a single power law.

record.verdict_notes: Perplexity must be converted to log perplexity when judging V4's loss magnitude. Small measurable architecture gains do not contradict 'changes loss only slightly.' Figure 2's unavailable values and the limited architecture range are not evidence for limits_scope. Tables 3–10 and Appendix C are explicitly declared in rows_left_out, so they are not missing extractions. The initialization-dependent architecture ranking does not itself test V7's claims about fitted scaling laws. No uncertainty estimates establish statistical equivalence.

versions.untested_parts: No power-law fits of held-out loss against parameters, tokens, or compute; no multi-order-of-magnitude scaling test.
No predictions from small runs compared with larger runs.
No fixed-compute optimization or fitted parameter/token allocation trends.
Does not vary width or explore a wide range of architecture families; tested comparisons are limited to the reported Transformer, mHC, Looped, and Hyperloop configurations.
No other modalities or regimes such as fine-tuning or transfer are tested.
Reports aggregate downstream accuracy at three model-size settings, but does not fit a predictive relationship to pretraining loss or use smaller runs to predict larger-run task performance.
Does not compare scaling-law exponents or fitting choices, or test whether loss curves bend away from power laws.

relationships.condition: Nearly parameter-matched Transformer/mHC and Looped/Hyperloop comparisons, BF16, three Table 1 settings
relationships.reason: R01–R12 show small cross-entropy differences: approximately 0.003–0.038 nats/token within matched pairs; lower Hyperloop perplexity alone is not the supporting criterion.
relationships.display_finding: Matched architecture pairs differed in cross-entropy by approximately 0.003–0.038 nats/token.

relationships.condition: Nearly parameter-matched architecture pairs after INT4 quantization
relationships.reason: R13–R24 show architecture-related cross-entropy differences of approximately 0.008–0.043 nats/token, small relative to losses around 2.15–2.72 nats/token.
relationships.display_finding: Architecture-related cross-entropy differences were approximately 0.008–0.043 nats/token against losses around 2.15–2.72 nats/token.

relationships.condition: Smallest architecture pairs trained on 100B tokens
relationships.reason: R37–R40 give PPL 12.15/12.16 for Transformer/mHC and 12.56/12.19 for Looped/Hyperloop, with matched-pair loss gaps at most approximately 0.030 nats/token.
relationships.display_finding: Transformer/mHC perplexities were 12.15/12.16 and Looped/Hyperloop perplexities were 12.56/12.19, with matched-pair loss gaps at most approximately 0.030 nats/token.

relationships.condition: Average downstream accuracy as parameters and training tokens increase across three settings within each architecture family
relationships.reason: R25–R36 show monotonic average-accuracy gains in all four families, from about 41% to 48–50% to 53–55%; this supports the scale trend without validating quantitative predictions.
relationships.display_finding: Average accuracy increased monotonically across three settings in all four families, from about 41% to 48–50% to 53–55%, without validated quantitative forecasts.
